nodes.description:
The defining measurement of the disease, and the one that names it. In the index siblings the fractional catabolic rate of IgG was about five times normal while synthesis was normal - so the low serum concentrations are a clearance phenotype, not a production phenotype.
The two classical alternative causes of low serum protein were excluded by direct measurement rather than by inference: there was no proteinuria, and faecal chromium-labelled albumin studies were normal, ruling out gastrointestinal loss. That exclusion is what made "hypercatabolic" a claim about mechanism rather than a label for unexplained hypoproteinaemia.
nodes.id: Accelerated Endogenous Catabolism of IgG and Albumin

nodes.description:
Both described families are consanguineous and the variants are homozygous. In the family that defined the disease the lesion is a single nucleotide transversion replacing a conserved alanine with proline in the middle of the beta-2-microglobulin signal sequence - that is, it does not alter the mature protein at all, it prevents the protein from being made properly in the first place.
The signal-peptide position matters for how the entry is read downstream. This is not an allele that produces a subtly altered beta-2-microglobulin which then fails to bind one particular heavy chain; it lowers the supply of the light chain itself, which is why every heterodimer that needs it is affected together.

nodes.description:
Beta-2-microglobulin is not a component of one receptor; it is the non-polymorphic light chain of the whole MHC class I fold. Classical HLA-A/B/C, the lipid-presenting CD1 molecules, and FcRn are all heterodimers of a class-I-like heavy chain with the same light chain, so a shortage of it destabilises all of them at once.
This node is the reason the disease has two arms rather than one, and it is why the immunological defect is broader than in the commoner TAP-deficient form of MHC class I deficiency: TAP loss leaves the heterodimer intact and starves it of peptide, whereas beta-2-microglobulin loss removes the shared subunit that CD1 and FcRn need too.
nodes.id: Depletion of the Shared MHC Class I Light Chain

nodes.description:
Two lymphocyte compartments are shaped by surface class I and both are abnormal. The conventional CD8 alpha-beta T cell compartment fails, and CD8-positive gamma-delta T cells expand strongly in its place - the same substitution seen in TAP deficiency. NK cells are present in normal numbers but are not licensed, a state in which the cells exist and can be counted but have not been educated by class I to kill.
The NK finding is the reason a cell count is not a sufficient investigation here. A normal NK number and an absent NK function are the same laboratory result unless licensing is specifically assessed.

nodes.description:
The salvage cycle is a pH switch. IgG and albumin are pinocytosed indiscriminately along with other plasma proteins; in the acidified endosome FcRn binds them, and everything it does not bind continues to the lysosome. Returned to the neutral pH of the cell surface, the ligands are released back into the circulation. This is the whole mechanism by which two proteins get half-lives of about three weeks when comparable plasma proteins get days.
Two features of the receptor explain the shape of this disease. It binds IgG and albumin at separate sites, so one lesion in the shared receptor takes out both ligands without either competing with the other; and because the receptor pool is finite, the system is concentration-dependent, which is why catabolic rate rather than synthetic rate is the variable that moves.
nodes.id: Failure of pH-Dependent FcRn Salvage of IgG and Albumin

nodes.description: The controlled complement of the beta-2-microglobulin strain. Deleting the FcRn heavy chain leaves the rest of the MHC class I fold intact, so any phenotype it shares with the beta-2-microglobulin knockout is attributable to FcRn rather than to class I generally.

The biochemical endpoint. Because the receptor pool is finite and shared, heterozygous carriers sit on a gradient rather than a threshold: eight relatives of the index siblings were moderately IgG-deficient, while the parents in the second family were normal on every tested parameter except B2M message. The gene is dose-sensitive but the clinical phenotype is not simply proportional to dose.

nodes.description:
The antigen-presentation arm. Both the peptide-presenting classical class I molecules and the lipid-presenting CD1a, CD1b and CD1c disappear from the cell surface, because all of them are built on the same light chain.
This arm was invisible for the first twenty-five years of the disease's history. The 1990 protein-turnover study did not look for it, and the 2006 sequencing study measured serum HLA but did not characterise the cellular compartments; the immunological phenotype was described only in 2015.

nodes.description: The clinical endpoint, and it is strikingly variable within a single genotype. In the 2015 family the sister had recurrent respiratory infection and severe skin disease while her brother, carrying the same homozygous defect, was largely asymptomatic and was found to have bronchiectasis. Bronchiectasis in an otherwise well sibling is the reminder that structural lung damage here can accumulate without a symptomatic infection history.
